title: Which books are worth reading for case interviews and consulting?
description: A short, honest list of books that help with case interviews, structured communication and business thinking, and how to use each one.
hook: You do not need a shelf of books to prepare for case interviews. Practice matters far more than reading. But a few books are genuinely useful, especially early on or for building business judgement. Here is a short list and what each is good for.
body:
For case interviews

  • Case in Point by Marc Cosentino. A long-standing introduction to case interviews, with many frameworks and practice cases. Useful early on; avoid memorising its frameworks rigidly.
  • Case Interview Secrets by Victor Cheng. Clear on the thinking behind cases, especially hypotheses and driving the conversation.

For structured communication

  • The Pyramid Principle by Barbara Minto. The classic on answer-first, structured communication used across consulting. Dense but powerful. Our plain-English summary.
  • The McKinsey Way by Ethan Rasiel. A short, readable look at how consultants approach problems and work.

For business judgement

  • Good Strategy/Bad Strategy by Richard Rumelt. How to diagnose a challenge and choose a focused response.
  • The Personal MBA by Josh Kaufman. A broad, friendly introduction to business ideas.
  • Blitzscaling by Reid Hoffman and Chris Yeh. Business models, scale and network effects.

How to read for case prep

Read one case-prep book early, then spend most of your time practising cases out loud. Keep a business book going in the background for vocabulary and examples, a chapter a day.
